name: Sanskrit
notes: Classical Sanskrit (Pāṇinian standard, c. 4th c. BCE onward). Five-point place-of-articulation system: velar, palatal, retroflex, dental, labial. Four-way laryngeal contrast (plain/aspirated × voiced/voiceless). No short /e/ or /o/ (only long). ⟨व⟩ = [ʋ] labiodental approximant. Sandhi rules are extensive but modeled at the allophone level here. Short ⟨अ⟩ (inherent vowel) is [ɐ], not a genuine mid-central schwa [ə]: Whitney's Sanskrit Grammar (1889) §21 describes it as the "neutral vowel", equating it to "English so-called short u, of but, son, blood" — a near-open central/back vowel, not the higher, laxer schwa of unstressed English syllables. Long ⟨आ⟩ is correspondingly [ɑː]: Whitney §19 places it "in the 'Continental' or 'Italian' manner — as in far or farther", i.e. a fully back open vowel, distinct in quality from short a, not merely longer. ⟨र⟩ is not a trill: Whitney §52 states it "resembles the English smooth r, and, like this, seems to have been untrilled", and §52a that "no authority hints at a vibration as belonging to it" — this only rules out the trill [r] this spec previously shipped, since Whitney's nineteenth-century articulatory terms do not distinguish a tap from an approximant. The specific value [ɾ] (alveolar tap) rests instead on a measured argument, not this citation: in san_deva_broad.tsv, words containing ⟨र⟩ realise it as ɾ 6404 times, plain r 133 times, ɽ twice and never as an approximant. The conjunct ⟨त्र⟩ carries the same tap. The syllabic ⟨ऋ ॠ ऌ⟩ series is left as r̩/r̩ː/l̩ — the gold uses that same convention (r̩ 80, ɾ 3 in words containing ⟨ऋ⟩), which is the standard IPA notation for a syllabic rhotic and does not itself assert a trill vs. tap articulation the way the plain consonant symbol does. This spec reads ⟨ऩ⟩, ⟨ऱ⟩ and ⟨ऴ⟩ as their base letters ⟨न⟩ [n̪], ⟨र⟩ [ɾ] and ⟨ल⟩ [l], because the inventory has no separate phoneme for them. This spec has no ⟨ळ⟩, so ⟨ऴ⟩ takes the value of ⟨ल⟩.

sources.notes: 2nd ed.; consulted via the Wikisource transcription for the vowel-quality claims (short a as "neutral vowel"/short u, long ā as "far/farther") and for ruling OUT a trilled r. sources.author: The Unicode Consortium
sources.title: The Unicode Standard, Version 16.0, Chapter 12: South and Central Asia-I (Devanagari)
sources.notes: Rule R5: "In conformance with the ISCII standard, the half-consonant form RRA h is represented as eyelash-RA. This form of RA is commonly used in writing Marathi and Newari." The paragraph before Table 12-8: "Marathi also makes use of the “eyelash” form of the letter RA, as discussed in rule R5."

sources.author: The Unicode Consortium
sources.title: Unicode 16.0.0 NamesList.txt
sources.notes: U+0929 DEVANAGARI LETTER NNNA: "for transcribing Dravidian alveolar n"; U+0931 DEVANAGARI LETTER RRA: "for transcribing Dravidian alveolar r", "half form is represented as \"Eyelash RA\""; U+0934 DEVANAGARI LETTER LLLA: "for transcribing Dravidian l". Each letter is canonically equivalent to its base letter plus U+093C (0928, 0930, 0933), and is not a composition exclusion.
